# Question: generator shortcuts

The strongest plausible structural shortcut is **`global_dividers_only`**: treat only complete gray rows and complete gray columns as compartment boundaries, ignoring shorter gray wall segments. It fits every canonical demonstration because all canonical chambers are rectangular cells of global divider bands.

An exact disagreeing input is retained as case `global-dividers-only` in `repo/generators/529bd4803bcc/counterexamples/canonical_shortcut_witnesses.json`: generator seed `9`, sample index `2`, overrides `layout_kind=local_split`, `n_single=1`, `multi_seed_count=3`. The full 11×11 input, canonical Racket output, rival output, hashes, and command are in that JSON. The local vertical wall at column 1 in rows 6–7 separates an empty two-cell chamber from the adjacent chamber containing one blue seed. The intended rule leaves cells `(6,0)` and `(7,0)` at 0; the global-divider shortcut merges across that local wall and incorrectly paints both cells blue 1.

I checked the intended output with the selected canonical Racket authority using `arcpuzzles apply`; receipt: `checks/shortcut-witnesses/racket.json`, executed rule hash `222cee10aaec`, generator hash `c599785b…1cc2`. The proposed generator emits this family deliberately: `local_split` is every even schedule slot, the semantic census found the local-separator witness in 296/600 draws, and the 300-lesson rotation census found 0 ambiguities across 1,200 held-out positions against this and the odd-seed rival.

A second canonical-fitting rival, **fill every odd-seed chamber**, is also retained. Its three-seed case differs on 16 cells and is emitted by default in every generated scene.
